reasoning_traces.think:
The core thesis posits that reinforcement arises from the termination of a need-state rather than its onset. This implies a temporal asymmetry in reward processing where the cessation of aversive stimuli triggers stronger behavioral modulation. The mathematical framework treats reinforcement as a function of time-to-termination, R(T), which can be modeled as an inverse exponential decay with respect to need duration. Adaptive value dynamics suggest that while onset may initiate behavior, it is the resolution of need that optimizes long-term survival strategies. Thus, the value function V(t) = ∫ R(t') dt' becomes central to understanding how organisms learn to maximize reward through need-resolution. Conditioning strength C(H) reflects how hunger modulates learning efficiency, implying a non-linear relationship between physiological state and behavioral plasticity. These primitives form a coherent kernel for modeling motivational systems in both cognitive and embodied agents.
